lots.guide_summary: All surviving close evidence is Gowans SOLD hammer in AUD: $13 (single plated choker) to $60 (single plated chain), with mixed chain bundles at $30 to $40. One close ASKING lead (AUD 22 new, snippet only). Category guides: 9ct/14ct pearl pendants $50 to $80 hammer, an 18K one $150; rose-plated silver chain new GBP 29 (AUD 55 at 1.9096). No UNSOLD evidence.
lots.working: Gowans titled it plainly (no 9ct mention, unlike its gold lots), so treat as plated/costume plus silver chains. Keep: lowest close whole-lot SOLD is $30 (lot 411295, May 2026); 30 / 1.198 = 25.04, round down $25 (the $13 choker is one component only, not the lot). Flip: likely resale about $40 (top of bundle comps $30 to $40); less about 13% selling fees ($5.20) and $10 outbound postage = $24.80; / 2.396 = 10.35, round down $10. Upside only if the pearl pendant or chains test as 9ct gold, which is unproven.
lots.confidence_reason: Components clearly seen, but no carat or silver mark readable; Gowans comps are close bundles, not the same mix; pendant metal unknown.
lots.condition: Looks wearable; chains tangled, plating wear on the herringbone not visible at this size. One photo only, pendant back and clasps not shown.
lots.key_photo_findings: Stones & Silver ticket reads '18in 45cm', 'Trace RG 1mm 45cm/18in', '$28', 'AE035R-45' with a sterling silver roundel, so at least one rose chain is rose-plated silver bought new for $28. Pearl pendant is a half-round pearl in a plain yellow bezel; no stamp visible. Omega collar has a white-metal extender chain with lobster clasp. A second small bail with a clear stone sits near the ticket.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the pearl pendant (bezel or bale) or any chain stamped 9ct/375, 14k/585 or 925? Is the herringbone chain marked? What is in the small bag of grey chain pieces?

lots.guide_summary: Close SOLD evidence is all Gowans hammer: $35 and $45 for single cognac chip strands, $70 for an amber necklace and pendant lot. The top of the range is one close ASKING price, a dealer's AUD 382 for a vetted butterscotch chip strand, which is retail and optimistic. Category SOLD at Gowans runs $17 to $60; a live butterscotch bead strand is bid AUD 120 (not a sale). No UNSOLD evidence.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD is $35 (lot 433769, Aug 2026, single chip strand); 35 / 1.198 = 29.2, round down $25. This lot has more pieces and more butterscotch than that strand, so $25 is conservative. Flip: likely resale about $70 (top close Gowans SOLD for a combined lot); less about 13% selling fees ($9.10) and $10 outbound postage = $50.90; / 2.396 = 21.2, round down $20. Butterscotch could resell higher if proven natural, but no SOLD evidence shows that.
lots.confidence_reason: Clear identification of the pieces and three close Gowans SOLD results with photos checked; natural amber is untested and the chains' metal is unmarked, so not High.
lots.condition: All pieces appear whole; no visible cracks at this size; chains look intact with clasps. One photo only, no weight.
lots.key_photo_findings: Chip strand mixes opaque egg-yolk/butterscotch chips with translucent cognac, typical of natural Baltic chip strands. Loose pendant is a flat opaque butterscotch piece with swirl, top loop only. Curb chain carries a small round bead and a butterscotch drop; snake chain carries a small cherry drop. No hallmark readable on either chain.
lots.question_for_gowans: Are the two chains marked 925 or sterling? What is the total weight and the length of the chip strand? Any sign the amber is pressed/reconstituted (flow lines, bubbles in lines)?

lots.guide_summary: Close evidence spans AUD 83 to 430 but none of it is a recent sale: one close SOLD at $100 (Noble, 2018, white metal, over 24 months old), and ASKING prices of AUD 83 (new plated repro) and AUD 382 (new plated, UK supplier), plus a snippet-only lead of AUD 430 for a hallmarked 1904 silver one. Category: 2018 Noble sets on belts $100 to $120; a whistle-only estimate of GBP 40 to 60 (AUD 76 to 115). No UNSOLD evidence. Rates from open.er-api.com, updated 21 Oct 2026: 1 USD = 1.4286 AUD, 1 GBP = 1.9096 AUD.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD result in the last 24 months: the Noble lots are from 2018 and Gowans has no past lion-and-whistle lot. Keep and flip maxima are therefore 0. Old Noble results ($100 to $120 for white metal sets) and the dealer printout suggest a fair hammer of perhaps $60 to $120 if genuinely Victorian, but this is not SOLD-backed.
lots.confidence_reason: No hallmark readable, no recent SOLD evidence, and plated reproductions of this exact form are sold new.
lots.condition: Boss, chain and whistle complete and attached. Back of the lion boss (photo 5) shows a hex nut and bolt, a bent brass fitting and a pasted patch or label residue, so the fixings are replaced or later. Whistle shows wear and a small dent at the mouth; plating or patina wear consistent with age.
lots.key_photo_findings: Lion mask boss with chased scroll border, double belcher chain, cone whistle with stepped cap. Dealer printout from 62zmilitarycollectables.co.uk with the regiment name blacked out. Rear of boss has a modern-looking hex nut fixing and patch; no hallmarks visible on boss, chain or whistle in any photo.
lots.question_for_gowans: Are there any hallmarks or maker's marks on the boss, whistle or chain rings? Is it silver (a magnet/acid test or weight would help)? Does the printout show the regiment or the dealer's price? Does the whistle blow?
